results.name: span_boundary_gap
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples spanning at least 10, yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the range minus targets 1-10 outside it; the interval mechanism makes the range edge a sharp boundary, so observed below null_mean means people's generalization crosses the span edge more smoothly (similarity-like) than the model, above means a sharper edge.
results.code:
# name: span_boundary_gap
# description: For sets of 2+ examples spanning at least 10, yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the range minus targets 1-10 outside it; the interval mechanism makes the range edge a sharp boundary, so observed below null_mean means people's generalization crosses the span edge more smoothly (similarity-like) than the model, above means a sharper edge.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    member = dist == 0
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    outside = np.where(t < lo, lo - t, np.where(t > hi, t - hi, 0.0))
    base = (n_ex >= 2) & ((hi - lo) >= 10) & (~member)
    a = base & (outside == 0); b = base & (outside >= 1) & (outside <= 10)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: round_number_target_boost
results.description: For sets containing no multiple of 10, among non-example targets, yes rate for targets that are multiples of 10 minus other targets; the model gives multiples-of-10 rules ~zero posterior for such sets, so observed above null_mean means people endorse round numbers more than the model, below means less.
results.code:
# name: round_number_target_boost
# description: For sets containing no multiple of 10, among non-example targets, yes rate for targets that are multiples of 10 minus other targets; the model gives multiples-of-10 rules ~zero posterior for such sets, so observed above null_mean means people endorse round numbers more than the model, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    member = dist == 0
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    outside = np.where(t < lo, lo - t, np.where(t > hi, t - hi, 0.0))
    no_round = ~np.any(np.mod(ex, 10) == 0, axis=1)
    m = no_round & (~member)
    r = np.mod(t, 10) == 0
    a = m & r; b = m & ~r
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: same_decade_effect
results.description: Among non-example targets 1-9 away from the nearest example, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit (x//10) with some example minus when it does not; the model has no decade concepts, so observed above null_mean means people use decade membership more than the model, below means less.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_effect
# description: Among non-example targets 1-9 away from the nearest example, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit (x//10) with some example minus when it does not; the model has no decade concepts, so observed above null_mean means people use decade membership more than the model, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    member = dist == 0
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    outside = np.where(t < lo, lo - t, np.where(t > hi, t - hi, 0.0))
    same = np.any(np.floor(ex / 10) == np.floor(t / 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    m = (~member) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 9)
    a = m & same; b = m & ~same
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: single_vs_multi_example_near_generalization
results.description: Yes rate for targets 1-10 outside the examples' range on 1-example sets minus on 3-4-example sets; the size principle makes the model tighten with more examples, so observed below null_mean means people tighten less (or broaden) with more examples than the model, above means they tighten more.
results.code:
# name: single_vs_multi_example_near_generalization
# description: Yes rate for targets 1-10 outside the examples' range on 1-example sets minus on 3-4-example sets; the size principle makes the model tighten with more examples, so observed below null_mean means people tighten less (or broaden) with more examples than the model, above means they tighten more.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    member = dist == 0
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    outside = np.where(t < lo, lo - t, np.where(t > hi, t - hi, 0.0))
    m = (outside >= 1) & (outside <= 10)
    a = m & (n_ex == 1); b = m & (n_ex >= 3)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: small_target_bias
results.description: Among non-example targets more than 10 away from every example, yes rate for targets <= 20 minus targets >= 80; the model has no target-magnitude preference, so observed above null_mean means people favour small numbers as program outputs beyond what the model's concepts produce (below: favour large numbers).

# description: Among non-example targets more than 10 away from every example, yes rate for targets <= 20 minus targets >= 80; the model has no target-magnitude preference, so observed above null_mean means people favour small numbers as program outputs beyond what the model's concepts produce (below: favour large numbers).

    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    outside = np.where(t < lo, lo - t, np.where(t > hi, t - hi, 0.0))

results.name: within_item_agreement
results.description: Mean, over (set, target) items, of the pairwise agreement rate among the responses to that item; observed above null_mean means people are more consistent per item than the model (its per-item probabilities are too moderate, close to 0.5), below means people disagree more than the model allows.
results.code:
# name: within_item_agreement
# description: Mean, over (set, target) items, of the pairwise agreement rate among the responses to that item; observed above null_mean means people are more consistent per item than the model (its per-item probabilities are too moderate, close to 0.5), below means people disagree more than the model allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df.groupby([df["number_set"].astype(str), df["target"].astype(int)])["rating"].agg(["sum", "count"])
    k = g["sum"].to_numpy(float); n = g["count"].to_numpy(float)
    m = n >= 2
    k, n = k[m], n[m]
    agree = (k * (k - 1) + (n - k) * (n - k - 1)) / (n * (n - 1))
    return float(np.mean(agree)) if len(agree) else 0.0

results.name: magnitude_scaled_generalization
results.description: Yes rate for targets 1-10 outside the examples' range when all examples are >= 50, minus the same when all examples are <= 30; the model's intervals are linear and location-free, so observed above null_mean means people generalize further around large numbers (log-like magnitude compression) than the model does.

results.name: between_participant_breadth_sd
results.description: SD across participants (session blocks delimited by trial_index resets) of the yes rate for non-example targets outside the examples' range; the model has no individual differences, so observed above null_mean means people differ in how broadly they generalize more than the model's single shared observer produces.
results.code:
# name: between_participant_breadth_sd
# description: SD across participants (session blocks delimited by trial_index resets) of the yes rate for non-example targets outside the examples' range; the model has no individual differences, so observed above null_mean means people differ in how broadly they generalize more than the model's single shared observer produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    member = dist == 0
    n_ex = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    outside = np.where(t < lo, lo - t, np.where(t > hi, t - hi, 0.0))
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[1, (np.diff(df["trial_index"].to_numpy()) < 0).astype(int)])
    m = (~member) & (outside > 0)
    s = pd.Series(y[m]).groupby(pid[m]).mean()
    return float(s.std(ddof=0)) if len(s) > 1 else 0.0
